title: A `${…}` visibility predicate written inside `properties` is interpolated to a boolean before the visibility chain sees it, so no node-gate diagnostic can reach it
body:
## Where this came from

Measured while implementing #5687 (making a node-gate `data.*` predicate the adapter cannot answer emit a dev-only report). It is a **different silence** in the same chain, deliberately left alone there because the 2026-08-22 ruling on #5687 fences off interpolation ("no interpolation changes"). Filed unassigned for triage.

Duplicate search run before filing: semantic + keyword sweep of open issues over the properties hoist, the interpolation ordering, and the visibility-diagnostic surface (#5454, #5401, #4051, #3067, #5399) found nothing covering this.

## Facts (measured on `origin/main` 3ece13e33, plus `@object-ui/core`'s built evaluator)

`packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx`'s evaluation memo evaluates every `properties.*` value **before** the hoist that copies them onto the node. That ordering is deliberate and documented in place — *"Evaluating first is what makes one key mean one thing whether it is read as `schema.properties.x`, as `schema.x`, or as the `x` prop."*

Measured on `ExpressionEvaluator.evaluate`:

```
evaluate("data.status == 'draft'")    -> "data.status == 'draft'"   (string, verbatim)
evaluate("${data.status == 'draft'}") -> false                      (boolean)
```

Consequence for the two spellings of the same authored gate:

| authored as | reaches the visibility chain as | a node-gate diagnostic can see it? |
|---|---|---|
| `properties: { visible: "data.status == 'draft'" }` | the string, intact | yes — this is #5687's pinned repro |
| `properties: { visible: "${data.status == 'draft'}" }` | `false` (a plain boolean) | **no** — nothing is left to inspect |

The second row hides the block on every row exactly like the first, and the author gets no signal at all. Pinned as a known limit in `packages/react/src/__tests__/SchemaRenderer.nodeGateDataPredicate.test.tsx` ("KNOWN LIMIT, measured and pinned"), which asserts the verdict and the silence rather than papering over either.

## Why this is not just a `data.*` problem

The pre-interpolation is spelling-agnostic. Any predicate written as a `${…}` template inside `properties` arrives at the chain as an already-collapsed value, so **no** diagnostic that inspects the predicate at the gate — #5454's unresolvable-predicate reporter included — can ever fire for it. A `record.*` typo written as `properties: { visible: "${record.staus == 'draft'}" }` is in the same position.

This matters because `${…}` is not an exotic spelling. `@object-ui/types`' own protocol comments use it for exactly these keys:

```ts
hidden?: string;    // expression: "${data.role != 'admin'}"
disabled?: string;  // expression
```

## Scope note / why it was not fixed in #5687

Reaching it means adding a diagnostic **inside** the interpolation loop, gated on the key being one of the visibility keys. That is a small change, but it sits directly on the surface the #5687 ruling fenced off, and it needs a decision this card cannot take for itself:

- reporting there fires **before** the chain decides which leg is consulted, so a `properties.visible` that a co-declared `visibleWhen` outranks (#5454 leg 2) would be reported even though it decides nothing;
- the same loop carries genuine interpolations (`properties: { content: '${data.total}' }`) that must stay silent, so the check has to be keyed on the visibility key set rather than on the value.

Neither is hard; both are choices, not mechanics.

## Reproduction

`packages/react/src/__tests__/SchemaRenderer.nodeGateDataPredicate.test.tsx`, case *"KNOWN LIMIT, measured and pinned: a `${…}` template INSIDE `properties` is invisible to this leg"* — mounts the template spelling on two different rows, asserts the block is hidden on both, and asserts zero diagnostics. Flipping the expected report count from 0 to 1 is the failing reproduction.
